name: Ground Turkey Shepherd's Pie
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Classic 9x13 bake, weighs and divides cleanly at 14 servings, nothing in the catalog is a mashed-potato-topped turkey bake. Source prints 345 cal / 24g protein at 6 servings on a lean build; our standard build (2.5 lb turkey + real mashed potatoes + cheese) lands ~560 cal / 38g protein. Confidence: est_cal is our build, not the source's. | HARVEST: Mashed potato crust is listed as a prepared ingredient (4 cups), not built from raw potatoes.
intro_html: Shepherd's pie is what happens when a pound of ground meat and a sack of potatoes decide to become dinner together. Seasoned turkey and peas on the bottom, a thick blanket of real mashed potatoes on top, parmesan browned across the whole surface. Each serving carries 35 grams of protein and 569 calories for about $3.59 (at everyday cost). The potatoes are doing most of the heavy lifting on that price, and they are not shy about it.
ingredients_display: Cream of Chicken Soup (generic condensed (USDA)): 3.4 cans (1008 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Cream of Chicken Soup, 3.4 cans: ~$2.51. Buy 4 10.5oz cans: $2.96.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, ground nutmeg, dried thyme): ~$0.39. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $26.13 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.87 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $31.84 across 14 servings, roughly $2.27 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $18.49 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $50.33. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $3.59 a serving (at everyday cost) for a pan that eats like a Sunday dinner. Potatoes are the cheapest filling starch in the store, and this recipe leans on them without apology.
shop_smart: Buy potatoes in the big sack, not loose by the each. This batch runs through most of a 9 lb bag, so the bulk price is not going to waste sitting in your pantry.
93/7 ground turkey is the engine of this dish. The per-pound price drops as the pack size climbs, and turkey freezes clean, so buy the bigger pack and split it.
Frozen peas beat canned on both price and texture. The store-brand 12 oz bags are the play, and you need several, so check whether a larger bag is cheaper per ounce.
Condensed cream of chicken soup is just the binder here. Store brand does the identical job, and leftover cans sit on a shelf for a year without complaint.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and chunk the potatoes, cover them with cold salted water, and boil until a fork slides through with no resistance, about 20 minutes.
While the potatoes cook, heat the olive oil in your largest skillet over medium-high and brown the ground turkey, breaking it apart as it goes.
Add the diced onion and the garlic to the turkey, cook 5 minutes until soft, then season with salt, black pepper, and dried thyme.
Stir in the condensed cream of chicken soup and the frozen peas, let it bubble 3 minutes, then spread the filling into a greased 9x13 pan.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Keep them thick. Whipped potatoes will slide right off the filling.
Spoon the mashed potatoes over the filling and spread them to the edges so the pan is sealed, then drag a fork across the top to make ridges that will brown.
Scatter the parmesan over the potatoes and bake at 400F for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is browned and the edges are bubbling. Rest 15 minutes before you portion.
portion_html: Set the whole pan on the scale, subtract the empty pan weight, and divide by 14. Cut and weigh that number into each container so nobody gets the short square. Every serving lands at 569 calories and 35 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from masonfit.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: A full plate of meat and potatoes for about $3.59 a serving (at everyday cost), and this is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the whole library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, for $1 a month.

head.description: Ground turkey shepherd's pie meal prep: seasoned turkey and peas under real mashed potatoes with parmesan. 569 calories, 35g protein, about $3.59 a serving (at everyday cost).

recipeIngredient: 2.25 lb condensed cream of chicken soup
steps: Boil peeled, chunked potatoes in salted water until fork tender, about 20 minutes.
Brown the ground turkey in olive oil, then cook the onion and garlic in with it and season with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Stir in the cream of chicken soup and frozen peas, simmer 3 minutes, and spread into a greased 9x13 pan.
Mash the drained potatoes thick with salt, pepper, and nutmeg, then spread over the filling to the edges and fork ridges into the top.
Top with parmesan and bake at 400F for 25 to 30 minutes until browned and bubbling, then rest 15 minutes and portion into 14 containers.
